newsitem.title: ECUADOR: IMF mission due in Ecuador on Monday.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission due in Ecuador on Monday.

text.p: A mission from the International Monetary Fund is due to arrive in Ecuador on Monday to look over the country's fiscal accounts and analyze new economic measures by the government.

"On June 16, an IMF mission is set to arrive in the country. They are coming to look at the results of the previous economic measures and how the new measures will be implemented," Danilo Carrera, the President of Ecuador's Monetary Board, told Reuters.

On Wednesday night, Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon announced a package of economic measures including the trimming of profit margins in the petrol business and the reduction of electricity subsidies.

The whole package of measures is expected to boost government revenues by 1.9 percent of gross domestic product, allowing the budget deficit to be narrowed to 2.7 percent of gross domestic product by year-end from 4.6 percent currently.
The IMF's review will focus on the country's efforts in reducing the budget deficit, said Carrera.
"What we need (from the IMF) is a monitoring program that will serve to improve our country risk in the eyes of the international banking community," Carrera said.
